clue.text: An icicle perhaps

parts.note: an icicle is offered as an example of something defined by a temperature, the one at which dripping water turns solid

explanation.walkthrough: Strictly an icicle is not a temperature; the 'perhaps' warns that the clue is stretching the idea for fun.
explanation.definitionFit: An icicle only forms where water reaches the temperature at which it turns to ice, so the clue playfully calls it an instance of that temperature.

clue.text: Stockings used by anglers?

explanation.surface: A joke about what fishermen wear on their legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Open-mesh hosiery is called by this name, and a mesh for catching fish is literally what anglers might use.

clue.text: Successfully used a decoy duck?

parts.note: a decoy duck lures wild birds in, so using one with success means having lured or tempted something

explanation.definitionFit: To tempt or lure something to come closer is exactly what a hunter's decoy achieves when it works.

clue.text: Feature empty loop

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Feature empty loop' (5) for NOSE-around-O NOOSE: O (empty) inside NOSE (feature), but no clue word signals the container; a word is probably lost in OCR and no search found the printed text.

clue.text: They are used by plucky guitarists!

definitions.text: They are used by plucky guitarists!

parts.words: They are used by plucky guitarists!
parts.note: plucky normally means brave, but here it describes guitarists who pluck the strings, using small picks to do so

explanation.definitionFit: These are the small picks, the plural of a Latin-derived word, that players use to pluck strings.

clue.text: Decreasing press activity

explanation.surface: A newspaper industry in decline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decreasing' looks like 'getting smaller', but read it as de-creasing, taking the creases out.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as de-creasing, the first is removing creases with a hot iron; the second is the household chore of pressing clothes.

clue.text: Unreliable, having a crazy fit of rage first

indicators.note: first tells us the fit of rage piece comes before the others

parts.note: a fit of rage is a temper, as in 'lost his temper'
crazy means mental in informal speech

explanation.surface: Someone untrustworthy who flies off the handle before anything else.
explanation.definitionFit: A moody, volatile person or a machine that works only sometimes is described with this word.

clue.text: Added photo in place

parts.note: to place something is to set it down

explanation.surface: A picture has been added to the right spot on a page.
explanation.definitionFit: A small picture placed within a larger one, as on a map or page, has this name.

clue.text: Queueing for employment-and having a good chance of getting it?

definitions.text: having a good chance of getting it?

explanation.surface: Job hunters waiting their turn and hoping to be chosen.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally standing in a queue of applicants; idiomatically, being well placed to win a post.

clue.text: Supply space for the warehouse

parts.note: a supply of goods is a store
space, as in 'room to move', is room

explanation.surface: Asking how much space a warehouse has for its stock.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are places where stock or goods are kept until needed.

clue.text: Celt has removed the case

indicators.note: removed suggests the letters have been moved out of place and rearranged

explanation.surface: A Celtic man has taken away the case.
explanation.definitionFit: A school bag with a shoulder strap is a type of carrying case.

clue.text: Number 51 first made an opening print in a block

indicators.note: first places the 51 ahead of the number

parts.note: LI is 51 in Roman numerals
to make an opening with a blade is to cut

explanation.surface: A printing instruction about numbering and cutting into a block.
explanation.definitionFit: A design carved into a linoleum block and then inked to print is this kind of artwork.

clue.text: In net we contrived to do some weaving

indicators.note: contrived means cleverly devised, so the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: We made a net by weaving threads together.
explanation.definitionFit: To twist or interlace strands together is a form of weaving.

clue.text: Set to music and made a record

explanation.surface: A song was composed and then recorded.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing a tune down in musical notation is one sense; jotting something down for the record is the other.

clue.text: Head angry about bloomer

indicators.note: about here means scattered around, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A boss is cross about a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' looks like a mistake, the boss's reason for being angry, but it means a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloomer is a flowering plant, and this shrub has big round flower heads.

clue.text: Muslim ascetic shiver'd worryingly

indicators.note: worryingly suggests agitation, so the letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A holy man shivered with anxiety.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of a Sufi religious order vowed to poverty, known for whirling dances.

clue.text: An up-train?

parts.note: an up-train is usually one heading to London, but here it is taken literally as a train that climbs upward

explanation.walkthrough: In British railway usage an 'up' train travels towards London; here it means one climbing a hill.
explanation.definitionFit: A cable railway that hauls cars up a steep slope is literally a train going up.

clue.text: New look composer

parts.note: novel means new or original
lo is an old word meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: A new style from a composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivor Novello was a Welsh composer and actor, writer of 'Keep the Home Fires Burning'.

clue.text: Scottish essayist from said Cumbrian town

indicators.note: said tells us the town's name is spoken, giving another word of similar sound

parts.note: Carlisle is the county town of Cumbria, in north-west England

explanation.surface: A Scottish writer named after a town in the north of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Carlyle was a nineteenth-century Scottish historian and writer of essays.

clue.text: Rotter about to get behind the framework

indicators.note: to get behind places the word for about after the rotter

parts.note: a rotter is a cad, an old word for a dishonourable man
RE means about or concerning, as in business letters

explanation.surface: A scoundrel is about to sneak behind the scenery.
explanation.definitionFit: A core group of trained people forming the structure of an organisation is its framework.

clue.text: Offender cut lip badly right inside

indicators.note: inside puts the right letter within the mixed-up letters
badly signals that cut lip is rearranged

explanation.surface: A criminal who has been badly cut on the lip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' turns CUT LIP into CULPIT, and 'inside' puts R within it.
explanation.definitionFit: The person who committed a crime or wrongdoing is the guilty party.

clue.text: Went off for ten years as you might say

indicators.note: as you might say tells us the word is spoken, giving a different spelling

parts.note: a decade is a period of ten years

explanation.surface: Someone left for a decade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Went off' suggests leaving, but it means going bad.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that has gone off has rotted or spoiled.

clue.text: Go back without stopping taking one board game

indicators.note: taking means the shortened word takes in the letter for one at its end
without stopping means the word is cut short and its final letter removed

parts.note: to go back is to reverse
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Reversing nonstop with one board game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without stopping' takes the last letter off REVERSE, giving REVERS.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-player strategy game of flipping black-and-white counters, also sold as Othello.

clue.text: In the lair I sheltered the terrier

indicators.note: In tells us the answer lies inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A dog sheltered in its lair.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish is a breed of terrier, a red-coated dog from Ireland.

clue.text: Not allowed till ICI reorganise

indicators.note: reorganise means rearrange, so the letters are put in a different order

explanation.surface: An instruction that something is barred until a chemical company restructures.
explanation.walkthrough: ICI was Imperial Chemical Industries, a large British company.
explanation.definitionFit: Something prohibited or unlawful is forbidden.

clue.text: Medusa has sweet food perhaps before savoury

indicators.note: before puts the sweet before the savoury

parts.note: jelly is a sweet dessert
fish is a savoury dish

explanation.surface: A mythical Gorgon eating dessert before her main course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Medusa' suggests the Greek Gorgon, but it is a biologists' word for the sea creature.
explanation.definitionFit: Medusa is a zoological term for the free-swimming bell-shaped form of a sea creature with tentacles.

clue.text: Kingly blue

explanation.surface: A king in a sad mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Befitting a monarch is one sense; royal blue is a deep shade of blue.

clue.text: The banker rode about greatly hurt

indicators.note: about here means moved around, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A banker rode around after being badly hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: Being deeply upset by grief or loss is to be emotionally devastated.
